CHARACTER INFORMATION — EDIT ONLY THIS SECTION

CHINESE NAME:
[角色中文名]

ENGLISH NAME:
[Character English Name]


Use the provided TARGET CHARACTER reference as the primary and authoritative source for character identity.

The Chinese and English names defined above are the ONLY canonical character names used in the final artwork.

Whenever character-name typography appears visually,
use exactly the names defined above.

Do not invent alternate names.
Do not translate or abbreviate them.
Do not replace them with placeholder text.


Create a premium vertical Zenless Zone Zero character editorial poster combining:

a monochrome manga narrative collage,
traditional black ink-brush graphic energy,
multiple character close-up panels,
and ONE dominant full-color foreground character illustration.

The central visual concept is:

THE BACKGROUND TELLS THE CHARACTER'S STORY.

THE FULL-COLOR FOREGROUND CHARACTER REPRESENTS THE CHARACTER IN THE PRESENT MOMENT.

The result should feel like:

a dramatic character chapter cover,
a premium manga character feature page,
a limited-edition anime game poster,
and a stylized character archive page.

ASPECT RATIO:
9:16 vertical.


==================================================
1. CHARACTER IDENTITY — ABSOLUTE HIGHEST PRIORITY
==================================================

Use the provided TARGET CHARACTER reference as the authoritative source for:

facial identity,
face shape,
canonical eye shape,
canonical eye color,
hairstyle,
hair color,
bangs,
side locks,
rear hair structure,
signature ahoge if present,
hair accessories,
headwear,
ear accessories,
jewelry,
canonical outfit identity,
weapons or equipment where relevant,
body proportions,
signature visual motifs,
personality,
and canonical color palette.

The final foreground character must remain immediately recognizable.

Do not redesign the character into a generic anime protagonist.

Do not copy any identity,
face,
hairstyle,
clothing,
or color palette
from the stylistic example artworks.


==================================================
2. CORE VISUAL STRUCTURE
==================================================

Build the poster from THREE clearly separated visual layers.

LAYER 1:
warm off-white manga-paper background.

LAYER 2:
monochrome manga panels,
black ink brushwork,
graphic frames,
and character-name typography.

LAYER 3:
ONE large full-color target character in the foreground.

The foreground character must sit visually ABOVE all manga layers.

Maintain extremely clear hierarchy.

The foreground character should be:

sharpest,
brightest,
most saturated,
and most detailed.

The background manga collage should remain:

lower contrast,
monochrome,
slightly flatter,
and visually subordinate.


==================================================
3. BACKGROUND PAPER
==================================================

Use a warm desaturated paper base.

Possible colors:

ivory,
warm off-white,
pale parchment-beige,
soft cream-gray.

Keep it subtle.

Do NOT create dirty aged paper.

Do NOT add brown stains.

Do NOT add heavy rough paper texture.

The paper should feel like premium manga-print stock,
not damaged antique parchment.


==================================================
4. MANGA COLLAGE BACKGROUND
==================================================

Create several monochrome manga-style images of the SAME TARGET CHARACTER.

All manga panels should depict only the target character.

Possible panel content:

large facial close-up,
extreme eye close-up,
side profile,
serious expression,
calm expression,
battle-focused expression,
small half-body action moment,
weapon-preparation moment,
wind-blown hair moment,
quiet reflective expression.

Do NOT introduce unrelated characters unless absolutely necessary as indistinct silhouettes.

The target character should dominate all narrative fragments.


==================================================
5. LARGE BACKGROUND PORTRAIT
==================================================

Include ONE very large monochrome portrait of the target character in the upper background.

The face may be heavily cropped.

Possible crop:

eyes + forehead,
face from nose upward,
three-quarter facial close-up,
partial profile.

The portrait should occupy a large portion of the upper third.

Use:

black ink linework,
gray screentone,
white paper highlights,
soft cross-hatching.

Keep it behind all foreground elements.


==================================================
6. SECONDARY EYE PANEL
==================================================

Include one wide or diagonal extreme close-up of the target character's eye.

Place it around:

middle-left,
middle-center,
or another compositionally useful region.

This panel can be partially obscured by the foreground character.

Use the eye close-up as a strong narrative motif.

Preserve the target character's canonical eye shape even in monochrome.


==================================================
7. SMALL ACTION PANELS
==================================================

Include approximately 2–4 smaller manga panels.

Possible content:

weapon motion,
profile portrait,
upper-body battle pose,
calm side glance,
hair moving,
equipment close-up,
emotionally restrained expression.

Use irregular panel sizes.

Avoid making every panel a perfect rectangle.

Allow panels to overlap slightly.


==================================================
8. PANEL COMPOSITION
==================================================

Use energetic manga-page geometry.

Use:

diagonal panel boundaries,
cropped frames,
asymmetric placement,
layer overlap,
selected borderless panels.

Avoid:

perfect grid layout,
equal panel sizes,
clean corporate infographic structure.

The collage should feel designed,
but slightly explosive.


==================================================
9. BLACK INK BRUSH LANGUAGE
==================================================

Add expressive black ink brushwork around the manga collage.

Use:

broad dry-brush strokes,
black ink splashes,
sharp calligraphic sweeps,
rough brush edges,
controlled ink droplets,
large black directional marks.

The brushwork should reinforce the composition.

Do NOT cover the foreground character's face.

Do NOT turn the entire poster black.


==================================================
10. CONTROLLED INK TEXTURE
==================================================

Ink effects should be graphic and intentional.

Use several LARGE brush shapes rather than thousands of tiny splatters.

Avoid:

random black noise,
dense speckling,
muddy ink clouds,
dirty paper.

The ink language should remain bold and readable.


==================================================
11. MANGA RENDERING STYLE
==================================================

Render background manga artwork using:

clean black line art,
gray screentones,
controlled cross-hatching,
large black shadows,
white paper highlights,
simple manga shading.

Use strong facial drawing.

Do NOT make manga panels photorealistic.

Do NOT use grayscale 3D renders.

They should look genuinely illustrated.


==================================================
12. BACKGROUND DETAIL CONTROL
==================================================

The manga collage may be complex in composition,
but simple in local texture.

Keep:

faces readable,
eyes readable,
action silhouettes readable.

Avoid excessive micro-detail.

The collage must not become visual noise.


==================================================
13. FOREGROUND FULL-COLOR CHARACTER
==================================================

Place ONE large full-color version of the target character in front of the manga collage.

The foreground character should occupy approximately:

55–70% of the canvas height.

The character may overlap multiple manga panels.

The lower body may extend toward or beyond the bottom edge.

Use a powerful silhouette.

The foreground character should visually burst out of the manga page.


==================================================
14. CHARACTER-ADAPTIVE ACTION — MAJOR PRIORITY
==================================================

Choose the foreground pose according to the target character's personality,
combat style,
equipment,
and visual temperament.

Do NOT copy the exact poses from the style-reference artworks.

The pose should feel specifically designed for the target character.


==================================================
15. ACTION SELECTION — PERSONALITY LOGIC
==================================================

If the target character appears:

CALM / RESERVED / DISCIPLINED:

use a controlled combat-ready pose,
low center of gravity,
weapon held with precision,
quiet focused gaze,
minimal unnecessary movement.

COOL / ALOOF / CONFIDENT:

use a strong diagonal stance,
slight body lean,
one shoulder leading,
weapon or arm creating a bold graphic line,
calm self-assured expression.

ENERGETIC / PLAYFUL:

use a more dynamic forward or sideways movement,
lighter body posture,
larger clothing / hair motion,
playful but battle-ready expression.

ELEGANT / REFINED:

use flowing curved movement,
controlled hand placement,
long fabric / hair / weapon arcs,
graceful three-quarter pose.

MECHANICAL / TECHNICAL:

use equipment,
mechanical parts,
tools,
or weapon geometry
to form strong diagonal shapes.

AGGRESSIVE / DIRECT:

use a stronger forward-facing action silhouette,
weapon closer to foreground,
sharp body direction,
intense but controlled expression.

Choose ONE coherent pose language.


==================================================
16. NO GENERIC ACTION POSE
==================================================

Do NOT automatically use:

generic sword slash,
generic running pose,
generic crouching pose,
generic pointing pose.

The action should be informed by the actual TARGET CHARACTER.

If the character is not weapon-focused,
use body language,
equipment,
hair,
clothing,
or character-specific ability motifs instead.


==================================================
17. STRONG DIAGONAL MOTION
==================================================

Build at least one strong diagonal action line through the foreground character.

Possible sources:

weapon,
arm,
long hair,
coat tails,
ribbons,
mechanical equipment,
body lean,
leg direction.

Preferred major direction:

lower-left → upper-right

or

lower-right → upper-left.

This diagonal motion helps separate the foreground character from the vertical poster.


==================================================
18. CHARACTER SILHOUETTE
==================================================

The foreground silhouette must remain easy to read.

Avoid tangled anatomy.

Separate clearly:

head,
torso,
arms,
weapon / equipment,
major hair masses,
major clothing pieces.

Do not allow manga panels to visually merge with the character silhouette.


==================================================
19. CHARACTER COLOR EXTRACTION
==================================================

Analyze the TARGET CHARACTER reference and identify:

PRIMARY COLOR:
the strongest identity color.

SECONDARY COLOR:
the major supporting color.

ACCENT COLOR:
a smaller signature color.

Keep the foreground character faithful to these colors.

Do NOT automatically use blue.

Do NOT automatically use teal.

Do NOT recolor the character based on the example posters.


==================================================
20. COLOR HIERARCHY
==================================================

The overall poster should use approximately:

65–75%:
warm off-white,
black,
gray,
monochrome manga tones.

20–30%:
target character PRIMARY + SECONDARY colors.

5–10%:
ACCENT color,
small graphic accents,
lighting,
or equipment highlights.

The foreground character should contain almost all of the strong color.


==================================================
21. COLOR BLEED INTO BACKGROUND
==================================================

Allow only VERY SMALL amounts of the character's accent color to appear in the background graphic design.

Possible uses:

one thin manga-panel border,
one tiny underline,
one small geometric symbol,
a tiny brush accent,
small name detail.

Do NOT colorize the entire manga collage.

The monochrome-versus-color contrast must remain strong.


==================================================
22. FOREGROUND LIGHTING
==================================================

Use clean dramatic anime/game lighting on the foreground character.

Use:

clear facial illumination,
strong but controlled hair highlights,
well-shaped clothing shadows,
selected equipment highlights,
small rim-light accents.

The foreground character should visually pop from the paper background.

Do NOT overexpose the character.


==================================================
23. BACKGROUND LIGHTING
==================================================

The manga collage has no independent cinematic light source.

Treat it as printed artwork.

Use:

paper white,
gray tones,
black ink.

Do not apply colorful rim lighting to manga panels.


==================================================
24. DEPTH SEPARATION
==================================================

Create strong depth separation using:

color versus monochrome,
sharp versus flatter rendering,
overlap,
scale,
and contrast.

Do NOT rely heavily on blur.

Manga panels can remain reasonably sharp.

Hierarchy comes primarily from color.


==================================================
25. HAIR MOVEMENT
==================================================

Adapt hair movement to the selected personality and pose.

If the action is dynamic:

allow major hair locks,
ponytails,
braids,
ribbons,
or loose ends
to reinforce the movement direction.

If the character is controlled / reserved:

keep movement more restrained.

Preserve the original hairstyle topology.

Do not invent additional hair structures.


==================================================
26. CLOTHING MOTION
==================================================

Allow:

coat tails,
skirts,
ribbons,
sleeves,
fabric panels,
belts,
or accessories

to reinforce the selected action direction.

Do not create random wind.

Movement should follow the pose.


==================================================
27. WEAPON / EQUIPMENT
==================================================

If the reference character has recognizable weapons or equipment,
preserve their identity.

Use them as part of the composition.

Allow the weapon or equipment to extend diagonally across the poster.

Do NOT replace canonical equipment with a generic sword.

If no weapon exists,
do not invent one unnecessarily.


==================================================
28. CHARACTER EXPRESSION
==================================================

Adapt facial expression to personality.

Possible:

quiet determination,
focused calm,
subtle confidence,
restrained aggression,
playful confidence,
elegant composure,
slightly distant concentration.

Avoid:

generic shouting,
huge open-mouth expression,
random rage,
exaggerated smile.

The face should remain recognizable and controlled.


==================================================
29. LARGE CHINESE NAME TYPOGRAPHY
==================================================

Use the defined Chinese name as a major graphic element.

Place it in an upper corner or upper side area.

Render it using:

bold expressive Chinese brush-calligraphy-inspired typography,
high contrast black ink,
large scale,
strong vertical or stacked composition.

IMPORTANT:

The name must remain legible.

Do not invent extra Chinese characters.

The Chinese name may appear only ONCE.


==================================================
30. ENGLISH NAME TYPOGRAPHY
==================================================

Use the defined English name once as a smaller secondary identity label.

Place it near the large Chinese name or another quiet manga area.

Use:

clean uppercase or title-case Latin typography,
moderate tracking,
minimal serif or restrained sans-serif.

Keep it much smaller than the Chinese name.

The English name may appear only ONCE.


==================================================
31. NO RANDOM LEGIBLE TEXT
==================================================

Do NOT reproduce the Japanese text visible in the style examples.

Do NOT create random readable Japanese,
Chinese,
or English paragraphs.

Do NOT generate fake biographies,
weapon descriptions,
CV names,
or lorem ipsum.

Use ONLY:

the defined character names,
Zenless Zone Zero branding,
and non-legible decorative graphic marks where needed.


==================================================
32. DECORATIVE MICROGRAPHICS
==================================================

Instead of random text,
use small abstract editorial elements such as:

thin rules,
small boxes,
simple circles,
tiny geometric marks,
short nonverbal line clusters,
small emblem-like shapes.

Keep them secondary.


==================================================
33. ZENLESS ZONE ZERO LOGO
==================================================

Include ONE recognizable Zenless Zone Zero logo.

Place it in:

upper-right,
lower-right,
or another visually quiet corner.

Use a monochrome treatment:

black,
charcoal,
or pale character-accent color depending on background.

Keep it smaller than the character name.

Do not place it over the face.

Do not repeat it.


==================================================
34. ZZZ GRAPHIC INTEGRATION
==================================================

Integrate a subtle amount of Zenless Zone Zero visual language through:

small geometric UI-like marks,
restrained industrial linework,
tiny rectangular accents.

Do not overpower the manga / ink visual system.

The poster should remain primarily:

manga editorial collage + character illustration.


==================================================
35. COMPOSITION — UPPER THIRD
==================================================

UPPER THIRD should contain:

large monochrome face close-up,
major Chinese name typography,
one or two manga-panel fragments,
selected black ink brush strokes.

Keep enough light paper area for breathing room.


==================================================
36. COMPOSITION — MIDDLE
==================================================

MIDDLE section should contain:

eye close-up panel,
secondary portrait fragments,
diagonal manga framing,
beginning of foreground full-color character overlap.

Use this region to transition from monochrome storytelling into full color.


==================================================
37. COMPOSITION — LOWER HALF
==================================================

LOWER HALF should be dominated by:

the full-color foreground character,
weapon / equipment,
dynamic clothing or hair,
selected ink strokes behind the silhouette.

Do not overcrowd the lower corners with text.


==================================================
38. OVERLAP
==================================================

Allow the foreground character to overlap:

manga borders,
face close-ups,
brush strokes,
and paper graphics.

However,
do NOT allow black brush strokes to obscure:

eyes,
face,
important weapon grip,
or major identity features.


==================================================
39. PAPER / PRINT TEXTURE
==================================================

Use extremely subtle premium manga-paper character.

Possible:

barely visible fiber,
very fine printing irregularity,
subtle screen-tone effect.

Keep this texture restricted mainly to the monochrome background.


==================================================
40. FOREGROUND CLEANNESS
==================================================

The foreground full-color character must remain extremely clean.

Do NOT apply:

paper grain,
manga dots,
noise,
ink splatter texture,
or print degradation

across the character's skin and hair.

Background texture and foreground rendering must remain separated.


==================================================
41. MANGA SCREENTONE
==================================================

Use controlled screentone only inside selected monochrome panels.

Possible areas:

hair shadows,
cheek shadows,
clothing,
panel backgrounds.

Do not cover the entire page with dot patterns.

Avoid moiré.


==================================================
42. INK BRUSH DIRECTION
==================================================

Align major brush strokes with the foreground action.

If the character motion travels upward-right,
brush strokes should generally support that direction.

If the character uses a curved elegant movement,
use more sweeping arc-shaped strokes.

Ink should reinforce personality.


==================================================
43. PERSONALITY-ADAPTIVE GRAPHIC ENERGY
==================================================

CALM / DISCIPLINED CHARACTER:

cleaner panels,
long controlled brush lines,
more white space,
restrained splashes.

AGGRESSIVE / ENERGETIC CHARACTER:

stronger black brush bursts,
more dramatic diagonals,
slightly denser panel collision.

ELEGANT CHARACTER:

flowing brush curves,
balanced empty space,
refined manga crops.

TECHNICAL / MECHANICAL CHARACTER:

sharper geometric panel cuts,
more rectilinear graphic marks,
controlled industrial framing.

Adapt the entire poster rhythm,
not only the pose.


==================================================
44. VISUAL HIERARCHY
==================================================

Strict priority:

1. full-color foreground character face,
2. full-color action silhouette,
3. large monochrome background face,
4. large Chinese character name,
5. eye close-up / manga panels,
6. weapon / equipment,
7. black brushwork,
8. English name,
9. Zenless Zone Zero logo,
10. small decorative graphics.

Maintain this hierarchy clearly.


==================================================
45. CONTRAST CONTROL
==================================================

Keep background manga contrast strong enough to read,
but lower than the foreground.

Avoid pure-black manga masses directly behind dark parts of the foreground character.

Use paper-white gaps around critical silhouette regions.


==================================================
46. NEGATIVE SPACE
==================================================

Do not fill every region.

Preserve selected off-white paper gaps.

Use negative space around:

character face,
name typography,
weapon silhouette.

This keeps the composition readable despite collage complexity.


==================================================
47. CAMERA / FOREGROUND CHARACTER
==================================================

Use a dynamic but believable anime-game camera.

Depending on personality and pose:

slightly low angle,
subtle three-quarter perspective,
or controlled eye-level dynamic view.

Avoid extreme fisheye.

Avoid distorted anatomy.

The camera should strengthen the pose rather than become the subject.


==================================================
48. ANATOMY
==================================================

Maintain accurate:

face,
neck,
shoulders,
torso,
arms,
hands,
legs.

Correct five-finger anatomy where hands are visible.

Weapon grips must make physical sense.

Avoid twisted limbs caused by diagonal composition.


==================================================
49. CLEAN RENDERING / IMAGE QUALITY
==================================================

FOREGROUND CHARACTER:

extremely clean polished anime/game rendering,
smooth controlled color transitions,
clean cel-influenced shading,
precise facial features,
large coherent color regions,
smooth anime skin,
clean hair locks,
controlled shadows,
sharp equipment edges,
professional commercial finish.

BACKGROUND:

clean manga line art,
controlled screentones,
intentional ink,
off-white paper,
no uncontrolled noise.

Avoid:

digital noise,
film grain,
chromatic grain,
luminance grain,
random colored pixels,
dirty speckles,
heavy rough paper,
canvas texture,
random microtexture,
skin pores,
noisy individual hair strands,
muddy gradients,
blotchy shading,
dirty color transitions,
JPEG artifacts,
compression artifacts,
oversharpening halos,
excessive microcontrast.


==================================================
50. CRITICAL MANGA COLLAGE CHECK
==================================================

Before finalizing:

the background must clearly read as a collage of manga panels featuring the SAME character.

It should NOT read as:

random grayscale photographs,
random unrelated anime characters,
or generic abstract ink.

At least:

one large face,
one eye close-up,
and two smaller character panels

should be visually recognizable.


==================================================
51. CRITICAL COLOR CHECK
==================================================

The foreground character should be the primary source of color.

If the manga background becomes strongly colorful,
desaturate it back toward:

black,
gray,
off-white.

Only very small accent-color contamination is allowed.


==================================================
52. CRITICAL ACTION CHECK
==================================================

The foreground pose must feel appropriate to the TARGET CHARACTER's personality.

If the pose feels like a generic action-template pasted onto the character,
redesign it.

Use the character's:

temperament,
combat style,
equipment,
and silhouette

to determine movement.


==================================================
53. CRITICAL TEXT CHECK
==================================================

Use the defined Chinese name ONCE.

Use the defined English name ONCE.

Use ONE Zenless Zone Zero logo.

Do not generate additional random readable text.

Do not reproduce text from the style-reference images.


==================================================
54. CRITICAL CLEANLINESS CHECK
==================================================

Complex composition does NOT mean dirty rendering.

The poster can contain:

many panels,
ink strokes,
brush marks,

while still maintaining clean large shapes.

Avoid tiny random speckles everywhere.

Avoid texture overload.

Keep intentional separation between:

paper,
ink,
manga,
and full-color character.


==================================================
55. FINAL TARGET
==================================================

9:16 vertical Zenless Zone Zero character editorial poster.

One TARGET CHARACTER only.

Large full-color foreground character.

Dynamic personality-matched action.

Strong diagonal silhouette.

Canonical character identity preserved.

Canonical character palette preserved.

Background composed of multiple monochrome manga images of the same character.

One huge monochrome face close-up.

One eye close-up.

Two to four smaller manga panels.

Warm off-white manga-paper base.

Black and gray screentone artwork.

Bold controlled black ink-brush strokes.

Selected ink splashes.

Strong monochrome-versus-color contrast.

Foreground character sharp,
clean,
bright,
and saturated.

Background manga flatter and monochrome.

Large brush-calligraphy-inspired Chinese character name.

Small restrained English character name.

One small Zenless Zone Zero logo.

No random Japanese text.

No random biographies.

No unrelated characters.

No noisy paper texture.

No dirty grain.

No excessive microdetail.

Premium,
dramatic,
graphic,
manga-editorial,
character-focused,
chapter-cover atmosphere.


==================================================
NEGATIVE PROMPT / STRICTLY AVOID
==================================================

unrelated characters in manga panels,
different characters in background,
wrong character face,
wrong eye color,
wrong hairstyle,
wrong hair color,
character identity lost,

generic action pose,
pose unrelated to personality,
generic sword slash,
random weapon,
canonical weapon replaced incorrectly,
twisted anatomy,
broken weapon grip,

background fully colored,
colorful manga panels,
rainbow manga background,
background competing with foreground,

plain empty background,
no manga panels,
only one character on blank background,
ordinary game splash art with no collage,

perfect grid,
corporate infographic,
equal rectangular panels,
boring symmetrical manga layout,

random Japanese text,
fake Japanese paragraphs,
random Chinese paragraphs,
random English paragraphs,
Lorem Ipsum,

reproducing reference artwork text,
reference character names,
reference logos,
reference watermarks,

too many tiny ink splatters,

muddy black background,
ink covering character face,

CHINESE NAME:
[xx]

ENGLISH NAME:
[xx]


Use the provided character reference as the primary and authoritative visual identity reference.

The Chinese and English names defined at the beginning of this prompt are the ONLY canonical character names for this artwork.

Whenever character-name typography appears visually in the final image, use exactly the names defined above.

Do not invent alternate names.
Do not introduce alternate spellings.
Do not translate or abbreviate the defined names.
Do not replace them with placeholder text.


Create a premium vertical Zenless Zone Zero character portrait poster based on extremely low-key cinematic anime lighting and a narrow beam of naturally refracted sunlight.

The character exists primarily inside deep darkness.

Only a narrow shaft of refracted natural light reveals selected parts of the face, hair, neck, and upper body.

The central lighting concept should combine:

a bright predominantly WHITE natural-light core,

very restrained spectral coloration while the light crosses the face,

and progressively stronger wavelength separation as the light travels farther away from the facial focal region.

The result should look elegant, simple, optically coherent, and cinematic.

IMPORTANT:

Do NOT create a rigid seven-color rainbow stripe.

Do NOT create chaotic broken rainbow fragments.

Do NOT create multiple scattered caustics.

Do NOT cover the character's face with strongly saturated rainbow colors.

The face should primarily be illuminated by WHITE or warm-white sunlight.

Spectral dispersion becomes increasingly visible only farther away from the face.

ASPECT RATIO:
9:16 vertical.


==================================================
1. CHARACTER IDENTITY — ABSOLUTE HIGHEST PRIORITY
==================================================

Use the provided character reference as the authoritative identity source.

Faithfully preserve:

facial identity,
face shape,
eye shape,
exact eye color,
eyebrow shape,
nose proportions,
mouth proportions,
hairstyle,
hair color,
bangs,
side locks,
rear hair structure,
signature ahoge if present,
signature hair silhouette,
hair accessories,
headwear if present,
ear accessories,
jewelry,
neck accessories,
recognizable costume,
signature costume elements,
character-specific motifs,
characteristic proportions,
original visual personality,
and overall recognizable identity.

Do not redesign the character into a generic anime girl.

Do not copy the hairstyle, hair color, costume, or facial identity from the style-reference images.

The provided character reference determines:

CHARACTER IDENTITY,
HAIRSTYLE,
COSTUME,
ACCESSORIES,
ORIGINAL COLOR PALETTE.

The style-reference images determine only:

POSE,
FRAMING,
LIGHTING STRUCTURE,
DARK EXPOSURE,
REFRACTED-LIGHT AESTHETIC,
CINEMATIC MOOD.


==================================================
2. CORE VISUAL CONCEPT
==================================================

Create a dramatically underexposed anime portrait against an almost completely black background.

Most of the character remains hidden inside darkness.

Only a narrow refracted-light path reveals selected surfaces.

The portrait should rely on:

deep black negative space,
extreme low-key exposure,
large coherent shadow masses,
one narrow vertically oriented light path,
a bright natural white-light center,
subtle optical dispersion,
minimal ambient illumination,
strong cinematic chiaroscuro.

Approximately 70–85% of the visible character should remain in deep shadow or near-black values.

The final image should NOT resemble:

a normally illuminated character with a colorful stripe placed over the image.

Instead:

the light itself should be responsible for revealing the character.


==================================================
3. EXPOSURE
==================================================

Use intentionally low exposure.

Expose for the bright refracted light rather than for the entire character.

Areas outside direct illumination should appear approximately 2.5–4 stops darker than the directly illuminated regions.

Do NOT automatically recover shadow detail.

Do NOT brighten the whole face.

Do NOT illuminate the entire hairstyle.

Do NOT brighten clothing simply to display costume details.

Deep darkness is intentional.

Some hair, shoulders, and costume regions may disappear substantially into the black background.


==================================================
4. NO FILL LIGHT
==================================================

Use almost no conventional fill light.

Avoid:

front fill light,
beauty lighting,
softbox lighting,
broad studio illumination,
ambient face lighting,
global environment lighting,
strong bounce light,
HDR-style shadow recovery.

The shadow side of the face should remain genuinely dark.

One shoulder may nearly disappear.

Large areas of hair may merge into the black background.

Only extremely subtle reflected illumination may exist near directly illuminated surfaces.


==================================================
5. BACKGROUND
==================================================

Use an almost pure black background.

No visible environment.

No room.
No city.
No landscape.
No architecture.
No decorative fantasy scenery.

The background should feel like deep black empty space.

Use rich OLED-like black values.

An almost imperceptible undertone from the character's palette is acceptable, but the immediate impression must remain BLACK.

Large black negative space is essential.


==================================================
6. CHARACTER FRAMING
==================================================

Use a chest-up or upper-torso portrait.

Do not show the full body.

The character occupies approximately 65–80% of the canvas height.

Leave substantial black negative space above the head.

Show:

head,
neck,
shoulders,
upper chest.

Use a close cinematic crop.

The face remains the primary subject.


==================================================
7. HEAD POSE
==================================================

Use a graceful upward-looking pose.

The character gently raises the chin.

The face points diagonally upward, preferably toward the upper-left or slightly above the viewer.

Use a subtle three-quarter angle.

The neck extends naturally.

Maintain elegant believable anatomy.

The pose should feel like the character is quietly looking toward a distant light source above.


==================================================
8. EXPRESSION
==================================================

Use a restrained expression:

quiet,
calm,
gentle,
introspective,
slightly wistful,
serene,
mysterious,
softly distant.

Keep the eyes open.

The gaze should point slightly upward.

A very faint smile may be used when appropriate to the character.

Avoid:

large smile,
open-mouth laughter,
wink,
idol expression,
extreme surprise,
extreme sadness,
aggressive expression.


==================================================
9. CHARACTER-ADAPTIVE COLOR
==================================================

Preserve the original character palette.

Analyze:

hair color,
eye color,
primary costume color,
secondary costume color,
signature accent colors.

Do NOT recolor the character to match the example artwork.

Unilluminated colors become dramatically darker.

For example:

white hair in darkness:
deep cool gray,
violet-gray,
charcoal-white.

blonde hair:
muted dark gold,
deep warm brown-gold.

red hair:
deep burgundy,
black-red.

blue hair:
navy-black.

purple hair:
violet-black.

dark hair:
may almost merge into the background.

Do not preserve bright daytime saturation in shadow regions.


==================================================
10. PRIMARY LIGHT — NATURAL REFRACTED SUNLIGHT
==================================================

Create ONE narrow refracted shaft of natural sunlight.

Imagine warm daylight passing through a clear beveled glass prism or faceted transparent crystal located outside the frame.

The resulting projected light travels through the composition in a mostly vertical or very slightly diagonal direction.

The overall path should remain clean and visually simple.

Do NOT create a chaotic light pattern.

Do NOT create multiple separate spectral fragments.

The light may pass through:

upper empty space,
hair,
forehead,
one eye or the region beside one eye,
cheek,
jaw,
neck,
collar,
upper torso.

The exact placement should adapt naturally to the character.


==================================================
11. OPTICAL STRUCTURE — MOST IMPORTANT
==================================================

The refracted light should have THREE visual zones.

ZONE A — FAR ABOVE THE FACE:

spectral separation is visible,
but still elegant and controlled.

A mostly unified light beam begins to show:

a warm red-orange fringe on one side,
a pale yellow-white central region,
a restrained cyan-blue-violet fringe on the opposite side.

The colors remain soft and partially overlapping.

ZONE B — ACROSS THE FACE:

the different wavelengths overlap much more strongly.

The beam becomes primarily:

bright white,
warm white,
ivory,
pale golden-white.

Only very thin and subtle spectral edges remain.

The facial illumination should therefore appear mostly WHITE.

ZONE C — BELOW THE FACE:

as the light continues traveling away from the facial overlap region,
the wavelengths gradually separate again.

Color dispersion becomes increasingly visible across:

neck,
collar,
upper chest,
lower image area.

The farther the light travels from the facial overlap region,
the more visible the spectral separation may become.


==================================================
12. FACE = WHITE-LIGHT DOMINANT
==================================================

This is critical.

While crossing the character's face:

approximately 80–90% of the visual impression should be bright natural white or warm-white illumination.

Only approximately 10–20% should read as colored spectral edging.

The face must NOT look rainbow-colored.

The brightest area should appear:

white,
ivory,
pale gold,
warm sunlight.

Spectral coloration should appear mainly as:

thin red-orange edging,
very subtle cyan-blue edging,
occasional faint violet fringe.

Keep these colored fringes secondary.

The viewer should first perceive:

beautiful white sunlight across the face.

Only after closer inspection should they notice subtle prism dispersion.


==================================================
13. DISPERSION INCREASES WITH DISTANCE
==================================================

The amount of visible wavelength separation should depend on distance from the facial overlap region.

Near the face:

strong overlap,
mostly white.

Moderately away from the face:

slightly wider colored fringes.

Farther away:

clearer spectral separation.

This progression should be smooth.

Do not suddenly switch from white to rainbow.

Do not use constant spectral separation from top to bottom.

The optical effect should feel continuous and physically motivated.


==================================================
14. ABOVE-HEAD DISPERSION
==================================================

In the black negative space above the head, the refracted light may gradually reveal clearer color separation.

Keep the pattern clean.

Use approximately:

one warm side,
one bright pale center,
one cool side.

For example:

soft red-orange fringe,

bright warm-white / pale-yellow core,

subtle cyan-blue-violet fringe.

Do NOT show seven equally separated bands.

Do NOT create textbook ROYGBIV stripes.

The upper spectrum should feel elegant and photographic.


==================================================
15. LOWER DISPERSION
==================================================

After the light passes the face and travels downward across:

jaw,
neck,
collar,
chest,

the spectral separation may gradually widen again.

The lower section can contain more visible:

warm red-orange,
yellow-white,
green-cyan transition,
blue-violet edge.

However:

keep the white-light core present.

Do not allow the lower spectrum to become a fully saturated rainbow banner.


==================================================
16. SIMPLE SPECTRAL ORGANIZATION
==================================================

Keep the spectral structure visually organized.

Use one dominant warm side and one dominant cool side.

Suggested organization:

WARM EDGE:
subtle red,
soft orange.

CENTER:
warm white,
ivory,
pale yellow-white.

COOL EDGE:
soft cyan,
blue,
delicate violet.

Green may appear only subtly where the warm-white center transitions toward cyan.

This creates a believable spectrum without producing a rigid seven-color rainbow.


==================================================
17. NO TEXTBOOK RAINBOW
==================================================

Do NOT render:

seven equal stripes,
seven equally bright colors,
perfect red-orange-yellow-green-cyan-blue-violet bands,
perfectly parallel rainbow bars.

The spectral effect should remain partially overlapped.

The white center remains dominant.

Think:

natural sunlight with chromatic separation at the edges,

not:

a rainbow graphic.


==================================================
18. LIGHT-BEAM GEOMETRY
==================================================

Keep the refracted beam relatively straight and elegant.

Its overall trajectory should be easy to read.

Allow only subtle natural variation.

The light may:

slightly taper,
slightly widen,
shift a few pixels in direction,
soften gradually.

Do NOT create:

large zigzags,
chaotic curves,
fragmented patches,
multiple disconnected beams.

The beam should feel optically natural but compositionally clean.


==================================================
19. BEAM WIDTH
==================================================

Keep the total light path relatively narrow.

Approximately 5–10% of the image width is appropriate around the facial region.

The colored dispersion may become somewhat wider farther away from the facial overlap point.

For example:

FACE:
narrow white-dominant beam.

ABOVE / BELOW:
slightly wider spectral separation.

Do not allow the entire beam to become broad enough to illuminate half the character.


==================================================
20. EDGE CHARACTER
==================================================

Use:

a bright soft-white center,
moderately defined inner edges,
slightly softer spectral outer edges.

The white-light portion may have relatively clean boundaries.

The colored fringes should be softer.

Do not make every color edge razor sharp.

Do not blur everything into rainbow fog.


==================================================
21. SURFACE INTERACTION — CONTROLLED
==================================================

The light should respond naturally to the character's three-dimensional surfaces, but keep the effect clean.

ON HAIR:

the white-light core follows the broad shape of hair locks,

small spectral fringes may shift slightly along curved strands.

ON FOREHEAD AND CHEEK:

the projected light follows facial curvature gently,

without becoming dramatically distorted.

ON NOSE:

the nose geometry may create a small change in brightness or a slight local shadow.

ON NECK:

the light continues downward smoothly.

ON CLOTHING:

the beam follows major folds while remaining visually coherent.

Avoid excessive fragmentation.


==================================================
22. HAIR OCCLUSION
==================================================

Hair strands crossing the light may create small natural interruptions.

However, keep these interruptions subtle.

Do not shatter the beam into many separate pieces.

A few major locks may:

softly block part of the light,
produce a tiny shadow,
or slightly shift the local highlight.

The overall light path must remain visually continuous.


==================================================
23. NATURAL WHITE CORE
==================================================

The brightest part of the entire image should be the natural white-light core.

Use:

warm white,
sunlit ivory,
pale cream,
soft golden-white.

Avoid pure digital #FFFFFF everywhere.

Preserve a slightly warm solar quality.

The spectral edges must remain less luminous than the central white region.


==================================================
24. SATURATION CONTROL
==================================================

Keep spectral colors restrained.

Use natural translucent color.

Prefer:

warm muted red,
amber-orange,
soft golden yellow,
very subtle green,
gentle cyan,
deep optical blue,
soft violet.

Avoid:

neon red,
electric green,
laser cyan,
oversaturated blue,
synthetic magenta.

Brightness should be high.

Chroma should remain moderate.


==================================================
25. RAPID LIGHT FALLOFF
==================================================

Outside the direct refracted-light path, brightness drops quickly.

Do not use a large surrounding glow.

Do not illuminate the whole face through spill.

Do not illuminate the whole hairstyle.

Do not illuminate both shoulders.

A region only slightly outside the beam should already become substantially darker.


==================================================
26. FACE LIGHTING
==================================================

A large portion of the face remains in shadow.

The narrow white-light beam may illuminate:

part of the forehead,
one eye,
nose bridge,
one cheek,
part of the lips,
jaw,
neck.

Use strong asymmetry.

The light should create a clear vertical or slightly diagonal illuminated region across the face.

Everything outside it remains significantly darker.


==================================================
27. FACIAL SHADOWS
==================================================

Use large coherent shadow shapes.

The shadowed face should remain dark and clean.

Do not recover every facial detail.

Do not add bright reflected light to the shadowed cheek.

Do not add a strong rim light around the entire jaw.

Allow parts of the facial contour to fade into darkness.


==================================================
28. EYES
==================================================

Preserve the exact canonical eye shape and eye color.

If one eye lies inside the white-light region:

render it with high clarity.

Use:

clean iris,
precise pupil,
small white catchlight,
subtle warm reflection,
extremely restrained spectral edge reflection.

The eye should NOT become rainbow-colored.

If the other eye lies outside the beam:

keep it clearly darker.

Do not brighten both eyes equally.


==================================================
29. HAIR
==================================================

Preserve the exact hairstyle and hair color.

Use large coherent anime hair locks.

DIRECTLY ILLUMINATED HAIR:

reveals the original hair color,
bright white-golden sunlight,
subtle red/cool optical edging.

OUTSIDE THE LIGHT:

hair becomes very dark,
low saturation,
low detail,
possibly merging into the background.

Do not illuminate the whole head.

Do not add full-head rim lighting.


==================================================
30. LIGHT-COLORED HAIR
==================================================

If the character has white, silver, pale blonde, pale blue, or other light hair:

unilluminated sections must still become dark.

Possible shadow appearance:

charcoal gray,
deep cool gray,
violet-gray,
navy-gray.

Only directly illuminated regions should become bright again.

Do not let white hair glow everywhere.


==================================================
31. COSTUME
==================================================

Preserve the recognizable costume from the character reference.

Only directly illuminated fabric should reveal strong color and detail.

Unilluminated clothing should become:

dark,
desaturated,
near-black,
or silhouette.

The white-light core may illuminate a narrow section of clothing.

Spectral separation may become slightly stronger lower down.

Do not brighten the torso globally.


==================================================
32. SHOULDERS AND TORSO
==================================================

Keep most shoulders and lower torso dark.

One shoulder may nearly disappear into the black background.

Only the region crossed by the light becomes clearly visible.

Avoid full-body rim light.

Avoid bright outlines around both shoulders.


==================================================
33. OPTICAL CONTINUITY
==================================================

The entire effect must clearly originate from ONE refractive optical event.

The same general light path continues through:

upper negative space,
hair,
face,
neck,
clothing,
lower composition.

Its spectral separation changes gradually with distance.

The trajectory remains coherent.

Do not create unrelated patches of colored light.


==================================================
34. PHYSICAL OPTICS LOGIC
==================================================

Treat the character's face as being close to a wavelength-overlap / near-focus region of the projected refracted light.

At this plane:

different wavelengths remain strongly overlapped,
therefore the light appears mostly white.

As the projected light propagates farther away from this plane:

different wavelengths become progressively more spatially separated.

Therefore:

FACE = predominantly white light.

FARTHER ABOVE / BELOW FACE = increasingly visible dispersion.

This physical relationship is the defining lighting rule of the image.


==================================================
35. SIMPLICITY CHECK
==================================================

Keep the lighting elegant enough that the viewer can understand it immediately.

There should be:

ONE light path,
ONE white-dominant facial illumination,
ONE gradual spectral expansion.

Avoid complex optical patterns.

Avoid excessive secondary reflections.

Avoid multiple caustics.

Avoid scattered color fragments.

The final effect should look sophisticated rather than technically busy.


==================================================
36. ZENLESS ZONE ZERO LOGO
==================================================

Include ONE small Zenless Zone Zero logo.

Place it inside a quiet black negative-space region.

upper-right,
upper-left,
or another unobtrusive upper region.

Use a restrained monochrome appearance:

gray-white,
or an extremely pale version of the character's accent color.

Keep it small.

Do not repeat it.


==================================================
37. CHARACTER NAME TYPOGRAPHY
==================================================

Display the canonical English and Chinese names defined at the beginning.

Use exactly the defined names.

Place them in a quiet near-black region.

lower-left,
lower-right,
or another empty lower area.

Hierarchy:

Chinese name as the smaller supporting line.

Typography style:

clean contemporary sans-serif,
refined condensed sans-serif,
modern geometric typography,
minimal Zenless Zone Zero-inspired editorial design,
restrained letter spacing.

Use:

off-white,
soft gray-white,
or a very pale character-accent color.

Keep typography small and sophisticated.

Do not cover the face.


==================================================
38. COMPOSITION
==================================================

Use a 9:16 vertical cinematic composition.

TOP 20–30%:

mostly pure-black negative space,
light beam visible with moderately increased spectral separation,
small Zenless Zone Zero logo.

CENTER 40–50%:

character head,
upward gaze,
deep shadows,

only thin chromatic fringes around the facial light.

LOWER 25–35%:

neck,
shoulders,
upper torso,
deep shadows,
gradually increasing spectral separation,
minimal character-name typography.

Keep the composition simple and visually calm.


==================================================
39. VISUAL HIERARCHY
==================================================

Priority:

1. character face and eyes,
2. bright white natural-light region crossing the face,
3. deep cinematic darkness,
4. gradual spectral separation away from the face,
5. character silhouette,
6. character names,
7. Zenless Zone Zero logo.

The rainbow colors should NOT become the first thing the viewer notices.

The viewer should first notice:

the character,
the darkness,
the white sunlight.

The spectral colors should become a secondary discovery.


==================================================
40. ATMOSPHERE
==================================================

Overall atmosphere:

dark,
quiet,
intimate,
poetic,
dreamlike,
contemplative,
mysterious,
slightly lonely,
serene,
cinematic,
elegant,
restrained.

The refracted light should feel like a brief optical accident occurring inside darkness.

Avoid cheerful rainbow imagery.

Avoid colorful fantasy atmosphere.

Avoid festival-like colorfulness.


==================================================
41. RENDERING STYLE
==================================================

Premium high-end anime/game illustration.

Official game key-visual quality.

Use:

refined anime facial construction,
precise eyes,
smooth anime skin,
clean cel-influenced shading,
large coherent shadow masses,
controlled painterly transitions,
clean grouped hair locks,
high detail in directly illuminated areas,
reduced detail inside darkness.

Do not render every region with equal clarity.

==================================================
42. CLEAN RENDERING / IMAGE QUALITY
==================================================

Extremely clean polished anime rendering.

Use:

smooth controlled gradients,
precise facial features,
clean silhouettes,
large coherent hair shapes,
clear eyelashes,
smooth anime skin,
controlled color transitions,
clean shadow masses,

43. CRITICAL FACE-LIGHT CHECK
==================================================

The facial light must remain predominantly:

==================================================

==================================================

- and optionally the nose, cheeks, and mouth depending on what best preserves the character's identity.

The eyes should be the strongest visual focal point in the entire character area.

Use either:

- near-frontal view,
- or a subtle three-quarter angle.

The pose should remain calm and restrained.

- directly toward the viewer,
- slightly past the viewer,
- or slightly to one side.

Expression:

quiet,
gentle,
slightly distant,
poised,
introspective,
subtly mysterious,
emotionally restrained,
softly confident.

Avoid:

- exaggerated laughter,
- wide-open mouth,
- energetic idol expressions,
- exaggerated surprise,
- extreme sadness,
- exaggerated seductive expression,
- exaggerated action poses.

The visual language should resemble a poetic character portrait captured for a premium art book.

\==================================================
5\. CHARACTER-ADAPTIVE COLOR SYSTEM
===================================

IMPORTANT:

Do NOT automatically use the blue-and-white palette from the example artwork.

Identify three major color roles:

PRIMARY COLOR:
the strongest dominant identity color of the character.

SECONDARY COLOR:
the main supporting color found in the hair, clothing, accessories, eyes, or costume.

ACCENT COLOR:
a smaller distinctive highlight color associated with the character.

Build the entire poster palette around these colors.

Do not force unrelated blue tones onto non-blue characters.

Do not force gold onto every character unless it visually harmonizes with the character's design.

\==================================================

- soft ivory,
- warm pearl white,
- cool pearl white,
- pale cream,
- misty gray,
- desaturated pastel derived from the PRIMARY color,
- very pale version of the SECONDARY color.

Keep this region light and spacious.

Use very gentle tonal variation rather than a perfectly flat digital fill.

The upper region should create large areas of calm negative space.

\==================================================

=====================

- midnight navy,
- dark indigo,
- smoky violet,

- antique pale gold,
- muted rose gold,
- pale silver,
- platinum,
- cool metallic white.

- irregular thickness,
- broken sections,
- tiny gaps,
- subtle reflective highlights,
- uneven metallic accumulation,
- delicate handmade imperfections.

The foil must NOT appear as a clean vector outline.

It should not form a continuous glowing border.

Keep it restrained, refined and premium.

Avoid bright yellow-gold cartoon outlines.

\==================================================
9\. LIGHTING
============

Use soft cinematic anime portrait lighting.

The main light may appear to enter subtly through the torn opening.

Use:

- soft directional illumination,
- delicate highlights on the cheeks,
- subtle nose bridge highlight,
- controlled highlights on important hair locks,
- clear luminous reflections inside the eyes,
- extremely subtle rim lighting where appropriate,
- soft facial shadow transitions.

The face should be slightly brighter than the surrounding portrait environment.

The lighting should emphasize the eyes without creating harsh contrast.

Maintain soft atmospheric depth behind the character.

Avoid:

- neon lighting,
- cyberpunk lighting,
- rainbow lighting,
- extreme bloom,
- aggressive lens flare,
- harsh studio flash,
- hard spotlight,
- excessive rim lighting,
- blown highlights.

\==================================================

================================

Decorate the paper surfaces with extremely subtle line-art ornaments.

- tiny four-point stars,
- small celestial sparkles,
- constellations,
- orbital circles,
- crescent forms,
- astronomical diagrams,
- star charts,
- subtle geometric sigils,
- delicate floral line art,
- very thin ornamental curves,
- fine decorative vertical lines,
- restrained game-interface-inspired geometry.

Keep these motifs extremely faint.

They should normally use only a slightly darker or lighter variation of the surrounding paper color.

They must remain subordinate to:

1. the character's eyes,
2. the torn-paper opening,
3. the character-name typography.

Do not create a busy magical background.

Do not fill every empty area.

\==================================================

===============================

Include one tasteful Zenless Zone Zero logo.

- soft character-accent color.

- enlarge it excessively,
- repeat it multiple times,
- place it over the eyes,
- place it over the face,

\==================================================

===============

Overall emotional direction:

quiet,
poetic,
dreamlike,
mysterious,
elegant,
restrained,
introspective,
ethereal,
slightly distant,

rather than a standard promotional splash illustration.

precise eyelashes,
smooth skin,

CHARACTER NAME:
“[角色名字]”

OPTIONAL ENGLISH / ROMANIZED NAME:
“[英文名或罗马音；如果没有就删除这一行]”

Use the provided character reference as the primary and authoritative visual identity reference.

The character name defined above is the ONLY canonical character name for this image.

Use that exact name whenever visible name typography is required.

Do not invent alternate spellings.
Do not introduce unrelated names.
Do not repeat or reinterpret the character name elsewhere unless needed for visible typography.

Faithfully preserve the reference character’s recognizable facial features, face shape, eye shape and eye color, hairstyle, hair color, signature accessories, costume motifs, characteristic color palette, and overall visual identity.

Do not redesign the reference character into a generic anime character.

Create a premium painterly anime portrait with strong character-specific art direction.

## CHARACTER / POSE

Show the character in an upper-body composition, approximately chest-up or waist-up.

The character faces the viewer in a relaxed near-frontal or three-quarter angle.

Raise both hands naturally in front of the face and form a loose rectangular / camera-frame gesture using the fingers.

The hands should frame the eyes and central facial area without covering the character’s recognizable facial features.

Use:

- both hands clearly visible
- correct number of fingers
- believable finger joints
- natural wrist angles
- slight asymmetry between the two hands
- relaxed and character-appropriate hand placement

The gesture should remain stylish and visually strong, but its exact attitude should adapt to the reference character.

For example:

a lively / playful character →
make the gesture slightly more energetic, mischievous and spontaneous.

a cool / reserved character →
use restrained hand movement, composed posture and stronger visual stillness.

a gentle / elegant character →
use softer fingers, relaxed shoulders and graceful hand positioning.

a confident / assertive character →
use a cleaner, stronger framing gesture with direct eye contact.

Do not force every character into the exact same pose attitude.

The basic hand-frame concept remains consistent, while the body language should feel naturally appropriate for the reference character.

## CHARACTER-ADAPTIVE EXPRESSION

Do NOT automatically use a calm, melancholic or moody expression.

First analyze the visible personality and emotional impression communicated by the provided character reference.

Infer the portrait’s emotional direction primarily from visible character-design cues such as:

- facial expression
- eye shape and gaze
- eyebrow shape
- mouth expression
- hairstyle rhythm
- costume design
- color palette
- accessories
- overall visual energy
- pose language

Then adapt the generated expression to feel consistent with that character.

The final expression should feel like a natural extension of the reference character rather than a generic editorial expression.

If the reference character appears cheerful, lively or energetic:

use bright expressive eyes,
slightly raised eyebrows,
subtle playful smile,
light teasing energy,
more open facial expression.

If the reference character appears mischievous, cunning or playful:

use slightly narrowed expressive eyes,
subtle asymmetric smile,
playful gaze,
small hint of teasing confidence.

If the reference character appears cool, quiet or emotionally restrained:

use calm direct gaze,
relaxed mouth,
slightly lowered eyelids,
controlled facial tension,
subtle emotional distance.

If the reference character appears gentle, warm or elegant:

use soft eyes,
relaxed eyebrows,
very slight smile,
gentle gaze,
calm facial muscles.

If the reference character appears confident, strong or dominant:

use steady direct eye contact,
slightly sharper eyes,
subtle confident mouth shape,
controlled posture,
strong visual presence.

If the reference character appears dreamy, mysterious or ethereal:

use slightly distant gaze,
soft eyelids,
delicate mouth expression,
subtle introspection,
quiet dreamlike emotional presence.

If the reference character already has a very recognizable signature expression, preserve and reinterpret that expression directly.

## EXPRESSION CONSISTENCY

The generated facial expression must remain compatible with the character’s visual identity.

Do not impose:

sadness on a cheerful character,
a broad smile on a reserved character,
aggressive confidence on a gentle character,
blank melancholy on a playful character,
overly cute behavior on a mature or elegant character.

Preserve the emotional identity of the reference character.

The viewer should feel:

“this is how this specific character would naturally behave in this portrait concept.”

rather than:

“the same preset expression was applied to another character.”

## EYES

The eyes are the primary emotional focal point.

Preserve the reference character’s:

eye shape,
eye color,
pupil design,
eyelash style,
and recognizable gaze quality.

Adapt only the eyelid position, eyebrow tension and gaze direction necessary to express the character-appropriate mood.

Possible gaze directions:

directly toward the viewer,
slightly through the finger frame,
slightly sideways,
slightly downward,
or subtly upward,

depending on what best matches the reference character.

Do not unnecessarily redesign the eyes.

## MOUTH / FACIAL TENSION

Adapt the mouth expression subtly.

Possible treatments include:

tiny relaxed smile,
neutral closed mouth,
slightly asymmetric smirk,
soft parted lips,
subtle playful smile.

Keep expressions controlled and character-specific.

Avoid exaggerated open-mouth expressions unless the reference character is clearly energetic and expressive.

Avoid generic “sad anime face.”

## CHARACTER-ADAPTIVE COLOR SYSTEM

Do NOT automatically use a blue palette.

Analyze the reference character’s palette first.

Identify:

1. PRIMARY COLOR
The most recognizable dominant character color, usually derived from hair, outfit, or signature design.

2. SECONDARY COLOR
A supporting color from the costume, accessories, eyes, or secondary hair elements.

3. ACCENT COLOR
A smaller but visually distinctive color used in eyes, ribbons, mechanical parts, jewelry, trim, or signature ornaments.

Build the entire portrait around these colors.

Examples:

red-haired character →
deep crimson + burgundy + black / gray + restrained warm highlights

pink-themed character →
dusty rose + muted magenta + cream / charcoal

cyan-haired character →
ice cyan + pale blue-gray + deep navy + restrained yellow / gold accents

purple-themed character →
muted violet + lavender-gray + deep plum

green-themed character →
jade green + muted teal + dark charcoal + pale mint

Do NOT force the reference character into an unrelated color scheme.

## BACKGROUND COLOR

Create a simple minimalist background derived directly from the reference character’s palette.

Use the PRIMARY COLOR as the main background family.

Adjust its value and saturation so the character remains clearly separated from the background.

Recommended logic:

if the character has a bright/light primary color →
use a darker, muted version of that hue in the background.

if the character has a dark primary color →
use a lighter, softer or desaturated version of that hue.

if the character has multiple equally important colors →
create a restrained two-tone gradient or large soft color blocks using the two dominant hues.

The background should remain simple.

Possible treatments:

- smooth monochromatic gradient
- large soft color field
- subtle two-tone gradient
- faint broad painterly shapes
- very restrained atmospheric wash

Do not create a detailed environment.

No scenery.

No complex room.

No random objects.

The background exists only to reinforce the character’s color identity.

## CAP — CHARACTER-SPECIFIC COLOR MATCHING

The character wears a stylish baseball cap.

Do NOT always make the cap black.

Choose the cap color based on the reference character.

The cap should use either:

- the darkest version of the character’s PRIMARY COLOR,
or
- the character’s characteristic dark neutral color,
or
- the SECONDARY COLOR when it creates stronger visual balance.

Examples:

red / pink character →
deep burgundy, dark wine red, charcoal-red, or muted black-red

cyan / blue character →
deep navy, blue-gray, dark cyan

purple character →
deep plum, muted violet-black

green character →
dark teal, forest green, charcoal-green

white / silver character →
charcoal gray, cool gray, deep secondary accent color

The cap should clearly belong to the character’s own visual palette.

Add restrained contrasting stitching or small accent details using the ACCENT COLOR.

The front of the cap may display the text:

“ZENLESS ZONE ZERO”

in small clean lettering.

Keep the cap text secondary.

Do not let it compete with the character-name typography.

The cap should sit naturally on the head.

Preserve enough of the original hairstyle underneath and around the cap for immediate character recognition.

Do not completely hide signature hair accessories unless physically necessary.

## HAIR

Faithfully preserve the reference hairstyle.

Render the hair through large, coherent painterly anime locks.

Use:

clean major hair masses,
controlled loose strands,
broad expressive brushwork,
subtle edge softness,
character-specific highlights.

Do not turn the hair into thousands of individual realistic strands.

Do not replace the original hairstyle with a generic cap hairstyle.

## CHARACTER-ADAPTIVE LIGHTING

Adapt the lighting intensity and softness to the character’s emotional style.

The lighting color should still derive from the character-specific palette.

A lively character may receive:

cleaner highlights,
slightly brighter facial illumination,
more energetic accent light.

A calm or elegant character may receive:

soft directional illumination,
controlled highlights,
gentle transitions.

A cool or serious character may receive:

slightly stronger directional contrast,
restrained rim light,
deeper controlled shadows.

A dreamy character may receive:

soft diffused illumination,
slight atmospheric glow,
delicate edge light.

Always keep the face readable and attractive.

Do not let mood lighting obscure the character’s identity.

## PAINTERLY ANIME STYLE

Use a premium painterly anime / game illustration style.

Combine:

refined anime facial construction,
clean expressive eyes,
broad loose brush strokes,
controlled painterly shading,
slightly sketchy secondary edges,
softly simplified shadow masses,
selectively unfinished peripheral details.

Important focal areas should remain highly refined:

eyes,
face,
hands,
cap,
signature hair details,
important character accessories.

Allow secondary areas to become gradually looser:

outer hair,
shoulders,
clothing edges,
background.

The image should feel artistic and hand-painted without becoming dirty or chaotic.

Avoid heavy oil-paint impasto.

Avoid rough canvas texture.

Avoid uncontrolled scribbles.

## TYPOGRAPHY — USE THE NAME DEFINED AT THE TOP

Display the character’s name prominently as an integrated artistic typography element.

Use ONLY the exact character name defined at the top of this prompt.

Do not invent another name.

Do not create alternate spellings.

If an English / Romanized name was provided at the top, use that as the primary large wordmark.

Use the original character name as a smaller secondary subtitle.

If only one name was provided, use that single name consistently.

## TYPOGRAPHY STYLE

The name should look like deliberate graphic design rather than plain text.

Use a sophisticated artistic wordmark treatment inspired by:

modern Japanese anime key visuals,
fashion editorial typography,
game character branding,
music album cover design,
premium character posters.

Possible typography characteristics:

- custom stretched lettering
- elegant serif + modern sans-serif combination
- wide letter spacing
- overlapping letters
- partially cropped oversized letters
- thin outline typography
- subtle handwritten accent
- geometric letter construction
- controlled vertical / horizontal alignment

Do not make the lettering overly decorative or difficult to read.

The character name should remain recognizable and readable.

## TYPOGRAPHY COLOR

Automatically adapt the typography color to the reference character palette.

Possible logic:

dark background →
use off-white / pale character accent color for the main name.

light background →
use deep character primary / secondary color.

For selected letters or small details, use the character’s ACCENT COLOR.

Avoid unrelated rainbow typography.

The lettering must visually belong to the same color system as the character, cap, and background.

## TYPOGRAPHY PLACEMENT

Place the character name in an area that complements the portrait without covering the face.

Recommended placements:

- large partially cropped lettering behind the character
- lower-left corner
